numberItems.stem: Which inspection procedure does the handbook say to use on a combination vehicle?
options: The same 7-step procedure from Section 2, plus extra checks
A separate procedure that replaces the Section 2 method
Only a coupling check and a brake check
numberItems.explanation: Use the 7-step inspection procedure described in Section 2; a combination has more items to check and some new ones (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: During the walk-around, how much space should you see between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
options: A small gap so the plates can be greased
Enough to see the head of the kingpin
None
numberItems.explanation: Check that there is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: The fifth-wheel locking jaws should be closed around which part of the kingpin?
options: The head
The shank
The base
numberItems.explanation: Locking jaws must be around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin (p. 6-16, Figure 6.16).

numberItems.stem: Figure 6.16 labels the kingpin's parts. From top to bottom, they are the:
options: Head, shank, base
Base, shank, head
Shank, base, head
numberItems.explanation: Figure 6.16 labels the kingpin base (top, at the plate), shank (middle) and head (bottom) (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: What should you check on the **upper** fifth wheel (on the trailer)?
options: That all its locking pins are present and locked
That the glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged
That the air lines have enough slack for turns
numberItems.explanation: Upper fifth wheel: glide plate securely mounted to the trailer frame, and kingpin not damaged (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: What must you check on a **sliding** fifth wheel?
options: It is set as far forward as possible to shorten the rig
Its locking pins are pulled so it can slide during turns
It is properly greased, all locking pins are present and locked, and it is not so far forward that the frame hits the landing gear or the cab hits the trailer
numberItems.explanation: Sliding fifth wheel: not damaged, properly greased, all locking pins present and locked, no air leaks if air powered, and not so far forward that the frame or cab hits in turns (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: During the walk-around, the landing gear should be:
options: Fully raised, with the crank handle in place and secured
Raised just off the pavement
Lowered slightly so it can catch the trailer
numberItems.explanation: Landing gear must be fully raised with no missing or damaged parts, and the crank handle in place and secured (p. 6-16).

numberItems.stem: During the test that air flows to all trailers, what sends air into the **emergency (supply)** lines?
options: Applying the trailer hand brake
Pushing in the red trailer air supply knob
Pulling out the red trailer air supply knob
numberItems.explanation: Push in the red trailer air supply knob to supply air to the emergency (supply) lines; the trailer hand brake provides air to the service line (p. 6-17).

numberItems.stem: During the tractor protection valve test, the trailer air supply knob should pop out when pressure falls into the maker's range — usually:
options: 25 to 40 psi
Only once the tanks are completely empty
20 to 45 psi
numberItems.explanation: The control should pop out when pressure falls into the manufacturer's range, usually 20 to 45 psi (p. 6-17). One website gives 25–40 psi.

numberItems.stem: You are testing the **trailer emergency brakes**. The system is charged and the trailer rolls freely. You stop. What next?
options: Push in the trailer air supply knob and tug gently
Pull out the trailer air supply control and tug gently against the trailer
Shut off the engine and pump the brake pedal
numberItems.explanation: Pull out the trailer air supply control (or set it to "emergency") and pull gently with the tractor to check that the trailer emergency brakes are on (p. 6-17).

numberItems.stem: To test the **trailer service brakes**, you move forward slowly and apply the trailer brakes with:
options: The foot brake pedal
The trailer air supply knob
The hand control (trolley valve)
numberItems.explanation: Move forward slowly and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve), if so equipped; you should feel them come on (p. 6-17).

numberItems.stem: Static leakage test on a tractor pulling one air-braked trailer: engine off, brakes released. After 1 minute the pressure has dropped 4 psi. Is that acceptable?
options: No — the limit is 3 psi for a combination of 2 vehicles
Yes — up to 4 psi is allowed
Yes — up to 5 psi is allowed
numberItems.explanation: On the static test, pressure should not drop more than 3 psi in 1 minute for a 2-vehicle combination (5 psi for 3 or more). 4 psi is the applied-test limit (pp. 5-8, 5-10).

numberItems.stem: On the static leakage test (engine off, brakes released), what is the most a combination of **3 or more** vehicles may lose in 1 minute?
options: 3 psi
5 psi
6 psi
numberItems.explanation: Static test: no more than 5 psi in 1 minute for 3 or more vehicles (3 psi for 2 vehicles). 6 psi is the applied-test limit for 3+ (pp. 5-8, 5-10).

numberItems.stem: On the **applied** leakage test (engine off, foot brake fully applied for 1 minute), what is the most a **2-vehicle** combination may lose?
options: 3 psi
6 psi
4 psi
numberItems.explanation: Applied test: no more than 4 psi in 1 minute for 2 vehicles, 6 psi for 3 or more (p. 5-8). 3 psi is the static limit for 2 vehicles.
